Multi-Agent Delegation

Resource limits are becoming an authorization boundary for AI agents that delegate work across concur-
rent and failure-prone workers. Parent-child allocation constraints, affine objects, and distributed escrow
do not by themselves prevent overspend when replies are lost, effects complete after timeout, messages re-
peat, branches partition, or DAG joins alias one lineage. We formalize fault-tolerant budget conservation
for distributed multi-agent delegation. Budgets are quantized resource vectors represented by exclusive es-
crow credits that move through a delegation DAG. Before dispatch, a branch converts credit into an oper-
ation reservation bound to lineage, epoch, normalized effect, maximum charge, receiver, and idempotency
key. It persists a signed dispatch permit with quarantine; the gateway verifies that permit before first ac-
ceptance. Uncertain effects remain charged until authenticated settlement, a fenced authoritative no-effect
proof, or permanent retirement. We prove ownership partition, ledger and effect conservation, descendant
non-amplification, at-most-once settlement, late-completion safety, and partition confinement under explicit
mediation, durability, authentication, normalization, and gateway assumptions. An indistinguishability result
shows that partition-local availability requires exclusive preallocation. Bounded TLA+ checking, an indepen-
dent JavaScript explorer, and crash-injected two-process SQLite experiments exercise the declared scope and
detect timeout-refund and historical-certificate-validation mutants. The mechanism preserves the issued bud-
get bound across the evaluated crash, retry, duplicate, partition, join, and late-completion schedules.

1 Introduction
AI agents increasingly act as spenders, callers, schedulers, and delegators. A user may authorize a
procurement agent to spend at most $500, an incident agent to issue at most 20 production writes,
or a research coordinator to make at most 100 paid API calls. The coordinator can then create
workers, workers can create specialists, and multiple branches can converge at a final reviewer. A
scalar “remaining budget” is no longer a local counter. It is a consumable authorization resource
moving through a distributed, asynchronous delegation graph.
Here fault-tolerant means that the safety bound is preserved across declared crash and com-
munication faults. It does not mean every isolated branch remains available or every uncertain
operation eventually resolves.
Recent work makes important parts of this problem explicit. Agent Contracts defines multi-
dimensional resource constraints and a conservation law requiring child allocations to remain
within the parent contract [48]. Token Budgets documents 63 production budget overruns and
uses affine ownership to reject in-process aliasing, double-spending, and use-after-delegation [22].
AIP binds identity, attenuated authorization, provenance, and completion records across the Model

Approach. We model each root grant as a vector of quantized resources. The issuer creates ex-
clusive escrow credits. Delegation moves a subvector into a fresh child generation and atomically
removes it from the parent generation. A branch can spend locally during a partition only from
its exclusive escrow. Before dispatch, the branch durably creates a reservation bound to the root,
credit lineage, current epoch, normalized effect, maximum charge, receiver, and stable operation
key. Dispatch changes the obligation state but does not refund. Authenticated, effect-bound suc-
cess receipts are applied at most once; verified no-effect certificates return the reservation; irrecov-
erable uncertainty can be permanently forfeited but not silently reused.
Contributions. This paper makes five contributions:
(1) A fault-aware authorization semantics. We define resource vectors, exclusive credits, a del-
egation DAG, operation obligations, authenticated terminal evidence, and a transition system
that separates allocation, execution, settlement, and effect coverage.
(2) A fault-tolerant protocol. We give algorithms for idempotent split/delegation, local reserva-
tion, dispatch, terminal-evidence settlement, multi-parent join, recovery, epoch fencing, and
safe reclaim, together with refinement obligations for MCP/A2A/HTTP adapters.
(3) Conditional safety results. We prove ownership partition, global conservation, descendant
non-amplification, at-most-once settlement, effect-instance coverage, an external exposure
bound, late-completion safety, and partition confinement. We state an explicit trace-lifting
criterion that a concrete runtime must discharge before inheriting those abstract results.
(4) A coordination boundary. An indistinguishability argument shows why a shared, unallo-
cated unit cannot remain spendable in every partition without risking amplification. Exclusive
preallocation buys local availability; reallocation and reclaim may require coordination.
(5) An evidence-disciplined reference profile.We specify a provider-free artifact that connects
finite model checking, transition-level invariant checks, mutation, fault injection, and descrip-
tive local timing to explicit claims. Hosted-model quality and production deployment remain
outside the evidence.
Non-goals. We do not invent escrow, bounded counters, leases, Sagas, idempotency, transac-
tional tool use, commit-time authorization, or delegation tokens. We do not guarantee exactly-once
network delivery, roll back irreversible effects, infer prices, optimize allocation, tolerate Byzantine
infrastructure, or remain globally available through arbitrary partitions.

2.1 Resource-Bounded Agent Execution

2.2 Delegation Identity and Scope Attenuation
AIP supplies verifiable identity, attenuated authorization, provenance, and completion records
across MCP, A2A, and HTTP [36]. It carries abudget_usd ceiling that attenuates along a token
chain, but treats that value as a per-token authorization ceiling rather than a running balance; the
runtime remains responsible for aggregate spend enforcement. AATs let a holder derive a signed
chain with equal-or-narrower tools, arguments, depth, and lifetime without contacting the root is-
suer, while leaving transport binding deployment-specific [32]. Overlaying Governance formalizes
recursive delegation and scope composition over existing policy [18]. These mechanisms prevent
scope amplification. A consumable right adds a different obligation: two children can each hold the
same narrow scope while only one may consume the remaining unit. Offline attenuation alone
cannot decide exclusive ownership.
PAuth derives service-side slices for task-implied concrete operations and binds operand values
to provenance-aware authorization envelopes [44]. It strengthens operation-specific authorization,
but does not define exclusive ownership of consumable budgets, crash/partition credit transfer, or
settlement of an uncertain external effect.
Stateful least privilege makes authorization decisions depend on execution history and repre-
sents policy state as replicated state machines [9]. This establishes stateful cloud authorization as
a deployed security direction. Our state is narrower but structurally different: it tracks exclusive
consumable-credit generations and their effect obligations across an agent delegation DAG.
MCP standardizes model-to-tool connectivity and profiles OAuth authorization; A2A standard-
izes agent discovery and task exchange [1, 30]. MPAC adds multi-principal sessions, intent, opera-
tions, conflicts, Lamport-clock watermarks, optimistic concurrency, and governance [37]. We use
protocol adapters and causal metadata but do not claim a general coordination protocol. The active
individual Internet-Draft on Transaction Tokens for Agents propagates subject, actor, and agentic
context through multi-agent call chains [38]; it specifies neither a running consumable balance
nor exclusive escrow ownership or effect coverage.
2.3 Transactional Effects and Commit-Time Authority
Atomix gives agent tool calls progress-aware transactional semantics. It uses epochs, per-resource
frontiers, delayed commit for bufferable effects, and compensation for externalized effects [31].
Commit-time authorization separately requires fresh, causally prior, effect-bound, eligible author-
ity at the durability boundary [41]. Context-to-Execution Integrity binds protected fields, exact

Compensation is useful but weaker than prevention for irreversible payments, messages, disclo-

Two recent results sharpen this boundary. Machine-checked dual-write recovery shows that
source-side state alone cannot safely distinguish a missing sink write from a completed one and
formalizes recovery around sink acceptance records and fencing [3]. A cross-runtime study of
agent tool calls similarly finds that exactly-once behavior depends on the model, harness, and tool
contract, and that verification alone does not close late-commit races [28]. Our protocol adopts
that receiver-visible boundary and adds the invariant that every accepted or still uncertain effect
remains covered by exclusive credit.
2.4 Escrow, Numeric Invariants, and Coordination
The Escrow Transactional Method permits concurrent changes while reserving enough rights to
preserve numeric bounds [33]. Bounded Counter conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) build
on convergent replicated-data-type semantics and distribute decrement rights so disconnected
replicas can act without violating a lower bound [5, 43]. Just-Right Consistency combines CRDTs,
transactional causal consistency, bounded counters, and static analysis to synchronize only where
application correctness requires it [42]. These are foundational prior art, not our inventions.
Invariant confluence characterizes when valid divergent states can merge without coordina-
tion [4]. The recent Complete CALM criterion states a broader history-based boundary between
monotone specifications and those requiring coordination [16]. A consumable shared unit is non-
monotone: spending in one partition removes an option from another. Our protocol applies the
classical answer–exclusive preallocation–and then adds agent-specific delegation lineage, author-
ity bindings, normalized effects, and settlement obligations.
2.5 Leases, Fencing, and Durable Workflow
Leases provide time-bounded authority under clock and failure assumptions [14]; lock services
use monotonically ordered ownership and durable consensus to coordinate clients [8, 34]. Expiry
does not undo an already dispatched effect. We use an epoch as a fencing generation, never as
evidence that the previous effect did not happen.
Recent capability-coherence work maps authorization revocation to memory consistency and
reports an execution-count bound on post-revocation operations [35]. That revocation bound is
complementary: our epoch fence controls acceptance across ownership generations, while reclaim
also requires exclusive credit ownership and terminal effect evidence.
Durable distributed applications commonly decompose work into idempotent steps, stable re-
quest identifiers, and reconciliation rather than assuming a cross-organization transaction [15].
Stable call identifiers and duplicate suppression trace back to classic RPC semantics [7]; durable
systems additionally need the completion record and protected mutation to share the relevant
atomicity boundary. Linearizability remains the abstraction for an authoritative local transition
[17]; Lamport order supplies causal structure without pretending synchronized clocks determine
truth [24]. Table1 positions the resulting gap.

3 System, Failure, and Threat Model
3.1 Entities and Trust Boundaries
The system contains a root issuer, delegation controllers, agent runtimes, durable branch stores, ef-
fect gateways, a terminal-evidence authority, a reconciler, and an auditor. The issuer authenticates
a task grant and creates the initial budget vector. Controllers split and move rights. Agent models
propose work but cannot mint, settle, or refund credit. Each branch store atomically records local
ownership, reservations, outbox state, and terminal evidence. The effect gateway is the complete-
mediation point for a protected effect. It enforces the canonical operation key and epoch, and
returns or exposes an authoritative outcome.

ity, and reconciler form the declared enforcement trusted computing base (TCB); the controller
and reconciler are trusted orchestration but still cannot bypass store/gateway validation. A deploy-

3.2 Budget and Effect Surfaces
The protected budget is a finite vector over dimensions𝒦: currency quanta, paid API calls, risk
units, recipient-specific disclosures, or effect counts. Each dimension has an authenticated unit,
quantization, and maximum-charge rule. Cross-dimension exchange is disallowed unless a sepa-
rately authorized conversion contract is present; otherwise a dollar cannot silently substitute for
a risk unit.
Protected effects include any mediated external state change whose authority is consumable: a
payment, message, credential issuance, infrastructure write, record mutation, disclosure, or paid
call. Pure reads may still consume an API or disclosure budget. The normalizer maps protocol-
specific requests to a canonical effect descriptor. Effects outside the declared gateway envelope,
including covert channels and direct credentials, are outside the theorem.
3.3 Failure Model
The network is asynchronous. Messages can be lost, duplicated, delayed, reordered, or delivered
after an arbitrary partition. Processes can crash and restart, losing volatile state while preserving
completed durable commits. We do not use wall-clock order to infer whether an effect happened.
Clocks are used only for policy expiry under a stated deployment profile; epochs and authoritative
terminal evidence determine settlement.
The model includes concurrent fan-out and fan-in, duplicate delegation and dispatch, retries,
crash before or after each durable write, response loss, timeout followed by late completion, branch

3.4 Adversary
The planner, model, tool description, retrieved content, and downstream agent may be malicious or

3.6 Goals and Explicit Non-Goals
The safety goals are global ledger conservation, descendant non-amplification, at-most-once settle-
ment, continuous injective effect coverage, a root-bounded external exposure vector, stale-epoch
rejection, late-completion safety, and partition confinement. Concrete trace lifting is a separate
implementation proof obligation. Liveness is conditional: an online branch with sufficient local
escrow and a responsive gateway can progress without contacting the root issuer. A permanently
partitioned, escrow-exhausted branch can safely refuse forever.
The paper does not optimize allocation, predict token or price use, guarantee receiver honesty
beyond Assumption7, reverse completed effects, provide exactly-once network delivery, tolerate
Byzantine infrastructure, conceal accounting data from the evidence plane, or establish production
service-level objectives (SLOs).

4.4 Timeout Refund Creates a Late-Completion Race
Let an operation be dispatched before time𝑡, let no response arrive by𝑡 + Δ, and let the controller

gateway never executed and one in which it executed but the response is delayed. A refund is safe
in the first and unsafe in the second. No timeout value resolves the information gap. The system
needs a fenced, authoritative no-effect proof or must retain/retire the reservation.
4.5 Idempotency Keys Do Not Allocate Authority
A stable request key can stop the same receiver from applying one effect twice. It does not stop
two different operation keys from spending the same credit, a relabeled path from creating the
same normalized effect, or two receivers from interpreting keys in different namespaces. The key
must be bound to one credit generation, effect digest, receiver, epoch, and maximum charge, and
the gateway must enforce that binding.
4.6 Scope Attenuation Does Not Consume
A scope token answers which operations a child may invoke. It can be copied to two children with-
out widening the scope set, yet both children may spend the last dollar. Scope non-amplification
and resource conservation are orthogonal. We compose with AIP/AAT-style identity and attenua-
tion rather than replacing them.

4.7 Compensation Is Not Conservation
A Saga can schedule a refund after a duplicated purchase, but the duplicate effect occurred and
compensation can fail, cost money, or be semantically incomplete. Compensation is a valid re-
covery policy for designated effects; it is not evidence that the authorization budget was never
exceeded. We record compensation as a further effect with its own authority and accounting.
4.8 Independent Correct Components Can Compose Incorrectly
An allocation service, idempotent gateway, lease manager, and receipt verifier can each be locally
correct while disagreeing on operation identity or epoch. For example, a gateway may deduplicate
on an HTTP key while the ledger retries under a new operation ID; or a lease manager may fence
the branch while the receiver accepts the old generation. The protocol therefore requires one joint
canonical binding and a concrete-to-abstract refinement contract.
4.9 The Joint Conditions Are Individually Necessary
The external bound is not obtained by merely placing familiar components next to one another. It
uses four cross-component conditions on the same canonical operation:
𝒥 = ExclusiveOwnership ∧ InstanceInjectivity ∧ CompleteCharge ∧ FenceOrdering.
Each conjunct has a one-unit counterexample if omitted while the others are retained:

and each produces one correctly receipted effect;

stances while only one operation remains in the ledger;

one-unit effect, so internal settlement is conserved while actual cost is not; and
(4) without fence ordering, an old request can be accepted after its atom is reissued, then both the

8.5 Concurrency and Placement
Credits are the unit of locality. Operations on disjoint credits need no shared counter and can

nation is required to move unused rights between partitions, join credits at one authority, change
resource semantics, or reclaim a lost generation. This is the intended “just-right” boundary: spend-

9 Evaluation Methodology
The evaluation is claim-driven and intentionally performed after the model, protocol, theorem
assumptions, and failure semantics are fixed. This order reduces the risk of fitting definitions to
favorable measurements. The artifact uses no hosted model or provider. Agent decisions are deter-
ministic event generators because the evaluated claims concern distributed ownership and settle-

We use frozen cases, explicit oracles, and machine-readable denial reasons. The present oracle
is a distributed state invariant, and each paired variation is a crash, message, permit, or epoch
schedule rather than a natural language authorization context.
MAS-FIRE provides a complementary taxonomy and injection framework for semantic, cogni-
tive, and inter-agent coordination faults in LLM-based multi-agent systems [19]. Our evaluation
targets a different layer: durable crash cuts, duplicated or reordered protocol events, epoch fenc-

robustness.

11 Security Analysis
11.1 Safety Against a Malicious or Confused Agent
The agent is not trusted to report a balance, choose a credit generation, forge terminal evidence,
or decide that a timeout is a refund. It may emit arbitrarily many proposals, retries, delegations,
cancellations, and joins. The branch store accepts a proposal only if the current credit exclusively
owns the selected footprint, the label and joint witness authorize the normalized effect, and the
immutable operation binding either does not yet exist or matches exactly. Consequently, prompt
injection can influence the proposed action but cannot by itself duplicate a right.
A compromised worker can still waste its own authorized escrow by reserving unproductive
work, creating indeterminate obligations, or intentionally withholding completion. Conservation
is a safety property, not a defense against budget denial. Deployments need rate limits, per-child
reservation caps, bounded delegation depth, admission control, and human escalation for large or
long-lived quarantines.
11.2 Replay, Equivocation, and Identifier Substitution
Every transfer, operation, and terminal-evidence item has a stable identifier, but identifier unique-
ness alone is insufficient. The branch/gatewayenforcement verifier, which is inside the safety TCB,
recomputes the single canonical operation binding in Equation (6), including the selector schema
version𝜈sel, and rejects any field mismatch. Transfers use their separate domain-separated certifi-

Settlement also binds where unused rights may return. A target must satisfy Equation (7): it

11.3 Stale Generations and Split Brain
Epoch fencing protects against a lost controller or worker that later resumes. The critical check is
at the last trusted boundary before the effect, not only at the branch database. A gateway accepts
a new request for(𝑐𝑖𝑑, 𝜂) only while that generation is current. After an authenticated𝜂+ > 𝜂 is

If two authorities can independently declare themselves current for the same credit generation,
exclusive ownership is already violated. Consensus, single-writer placement, or another correct
ownership service is required within that authority. The protocol confines this requirement to
ownership changes; it does not solve consensus and does not claim Byzantine split-brain tolerance.
11.4 External-Effect Ambiguity
The most consequential attack surface is a receiver that completes work and drops or falsifies
the response. The safe response is not to guess. Under the fenced-queryable profile, reconciliation
obtains the recorded result. Under the receipt-only profile, missing evidence leaves the right inQ
or eventuallyF. Under self-report, only the internal ledger claim survives.
This tiering follows the same fundamental requirement as systems that provide exactly-once
RPC or workflow execution: a completion record must be durably coupled to the mutation or
returned by a cooperating transactional endpoint [27, 49, 54]. A client-side retry library cannot
manufacture that coupling for an arbitrary third party.
11.5 Underreporting and Variable Charges
A maximum reservation u is sound only if the gateway can prevent an actual charge above it.
For a paid API, that can mean preauthorization, provider-side hard caps, chunked metering with
renewal, or reserving the maximum billable unit. If the provider reveals usage only afterward and
may exceed u, no local algorithm can prove a hard bound on the real charge. The appropriate
choices are to refuse the hard-bound profile, reserve a conservative worst case, or state a softer
monitoring claim.
Partial settlement is safe when the receipt authenticatesd ⪯ u. The remainder returns only
after that receipt. For streaming calls, the gateway can use successive sub-operations with separate
reserved chunks; canceling a stream is not itself a zero-charge receipt.
11.6 Normalization and Path Aliasing
Two syntactically different requests may cause the same effect, while two similar strings may
address different recipients or preconditions.Normalize is therefore part of the trusted policy
boundary. Its test obligations include canonical encoding, default parameters, redirects, indirect
identifiers, locale and unit conversion, recipient resolution, protocol-specific retries, and relevant
domain preconditions. Unknown semantics fail closed.
Complete mediation is equally important [39]. An agent with direct cloud credentials can bypass
an MCP proxy; a browser can activate an effect through a UI path; a tool can invoke a second tool
internally. The theorem covers only credentials and routes that the deployment actually interposes.
Network egress policy, workload identity, receiver-side enforcement, and credential isolation are
deployment controls, not consequences of the budget data structure.
11.7 Audit Integrity and Rollback
A hash-linked log reveals deletion or reordering relative to a trusted checkpoint, but a compro-
mised store could roll back both state and its local log. Production profiles should bind store gen-
eration, credit epoch, and checkpoint sequence to a monotonic external witness, replicated log,
hardware counter, or consensus state. This strengthens forensic detection; exclusive ownership
still depends on the authoritative transition service.
Audit records contain sensitive purpose, recipient, spend, and graph metadata. The default evi-
dence plane should use digests and stable opaque identifiers, encrypt detailed receipts at rest, sep-
arate operational and audit roles, and enforce retention and deletion policies. Public verifiability
does not justify publishing task content.

12 Related Work Beyond the Closest Mechanisms
12.1 Agent Economies and Governance Receipts
EpochX treats tasks as bounties, supports recursive budgeted delegation, and uses lock and settle
operations [46]. It is therefore direct prior art for hierarchical economic allocation; our focus is the
failure semantics around duplicate delivery, persistent ownership, quarantine, fencing, and late
settlement that are not established by EpochX’s reported model and evaluation. AgentBound cen-
tralizes pre-execution governance and emits signed governance receipts [21]. Those receipts attest
to a policy decision, while our effect receipt attests to a receiver outcome and actual charge. Human
Delegation Provenance (HDP), a lightweight cryptographic protocol, provides human-delegation
provenance, while Aegon proposes ledger-bound tokens with attested receipts [6, 10]. We do not
claim the first delegation chain, ledger token, or signed receipt.
Agent Contracts and Token Budgets are the nearest resource-governance works [22, 48]. Their
allocation law and affine ownership discipline motivate our model. The contribution here begins
where one process or one allocation snapshot stops being authoritative: ownership must survive
messages, durable crash cuts, joins, and uncertain effects.
12.2 Authorization Delegation
OAuth token exchange and Rich Authorization Requests provide standardized building blocks for
audience-bound exchange and structured authorization [20, 29]. AIP and the current AAT Internet-
Draft extend these ideas to agent identity and attenuating chains [32, 36]; Overlaying Governance
formalizes policy composition [18]. These answerwhich actions remain permitted . Our credits add
linear consumption: two equally attenuated children must not both own the same last unit.

52 Zhu and Wang
Resource-bounded temporal logics have long represented strategies constrained by consumable
or producible resources [2]. Our problem is operational rather than strategic: it specifies how au-
thenticated rights move and settle under crash and partition. The logical connection is useful, but
a model-checking semantics does not supply durable message protocols by itself.
12.3 Escrow, CRDTs, and Mobile Rights
Escrow transactions reserve rights so concurrent transactions preserve a numeric invariant [33].
Mobile escrow distributes rights to occasionally disconnected clients [23]. Bounded Counter
CRDTs provide a particularly strong construction for partition-local decrement and rights trans-
fer [5]. Just-Right Consistency combines such mechanisms with analysis that coordinates only
invariant-sensitive operations [42].
We adopt, rather than rename, this lineage. The extension is that an agent credit carries an au-
thorization label and dynamic delegation lineage, the task graph can join without merging aliased
rights, and a spent unit remains coupled to an external-effect obligation through uncertainty. A
numeric counter that converges to a valid value can still miss a duplicated payment or disclosure.
12.4 Transactions, Workflows, and Exactly-Once Semantics
Sagas decompose long-lived transactions into steps and compensations [12]; Atomix specializes
transactional semantics to agent tool use [31]. RIFL couples request IDs with durable completion
records [27]. Beldi supplies fault-tolerant transactional serverless workflows, and ExoFlow targets
exactly-once DAG execution [49, 54]. These systems demonstrate that replay safety is a storage
and endpoint property, not a property of a prompt.
Our theorem is narrower in one dimension and broader in another. It does not claim a universal
exactly-once workflow. It proves at-most-once settlement and continuous charged coverage for
consumable delegated authority, including the safe but unavailable outcome in which an arbitrary
effect cannot be authoritatively resolved.
12.5 Coordination and Impossibility
CAP rules out simultaneous strong consistency and availability for every request during arbi-
trary partitions [13]; FLP limits deterministic consensus progress in an asynchronous system
with a crash [11]. Invariant confluence and the Coordination Criterion more directly character-
ize when application correctness permits coordination-free execution [4, 16]. Our Proposition1 is
an application-specific consequence: exclusive preallocation permits local work, while creating or
reallocating a shared spendable unit requires coordination or blocking.
13 Discussion
13.1 What Is Actually Conserved?
The object conserved is authenticated authorization capacity, not money or physical energy. A
dollar dimension means “authority to cause up to one dollar of charges under a named settlement
rule. ” If taxes, exchange rates, tips, later adjustments, or hidden provider usage are outside that
rule, they are outside the invariant. A rigorous deployment must define each dimension’s unit,
rounding, maximum charge, authority, and reconciliation semantics before issuing it.
The exact equality in Equation (8) is stronger and more diagnostic than merely checkingC ⪯ B.
It distinguishes spendable, moving, not-yet-exposed, uncertain, consumed, and sacrificed capacity.
Operators can therefore see whether apparent under-spending is true availability or merely hidden
stranding.

Fault-Tolerant Budget Conservation in Agent Delegation 53
13.2 Why Keep Both R and Q?
Combining reserved and indeterminate rights preserves the numeric equation, but loses a crucial
recovery fact. A durableR record whose outbox provably never became dispatchable can be locally
returned. AQ record may correspond to a real effect and needs external evidence. The separation
turns a crash cut into an auditable transition and prevents a generic “release pending reservations”
job from creating authority.
13.3 Safety, Liveness, and Economic Utility
The protocol’s safety is prefix-closed; its liveness is conditional. A branch can progress during
partition while it has suitable local rights and a reachable gateway. Once exhausted, it blocks even
if another partition has idle capacity. A quarantined right can remain unavailable forever. These are
not incidental implementation shortcomings but consequences of refusing to guess about exclusive
ownership or external effects.
Allocation policy can reduce the cost: assign escrow proportional to expected demand, keep
small emergency reserves in multiple zones, rebalance before known disconnections, and choose
queryable endpoints for large effects. Dynamic prediction may improve utilization but must not
enter the safety theorem.
13.4 Vectors and Conversion
Vectors prevent a worker from exchanging, for example, ten low-risk reads for one high-risk write
without authorization. Some applications legitimately convert resources: a dollar cap may pur-
chase token calls, or a global risk budget may be divided among effect classes. Such conversion is
a new protected effect. It needs a signed rate/rounding contract, consumes source rights, creates
target rights once, and preserves a declared value invariant. Without that extra contract, conver-
sion is undefined rather than inferred.
13.5 DAG Tasks, Forest-Owned Rights
Task dependencies and budget ownership should remain different graphs. A synthesis agent can
read results from many parents without owning their remainders. When it needs budget, each
input branch may transfer a disjoint credit or one authority may perform an atomic join. This
design prevents the common error of summing balances associated with incoming task edges.
At large scale, full atom-set proofs are impractical. Range certificates, bounded-counter rights
matrices, or cryptographic commitments can compress the footprint. The implementation must
nevertheless expose a disjointness witness and consume each input generation exactly once.
13.6 Standards Integration
The protocol does not require a new wire protocol. AIP/AAT or OAuth can carry identity and at-
tenuated scope; MCP or A2A can carry opaque credit and operation bindings; HTTP idempotency
or conditional writes can implement a gateway primitive. Standardization value lies in a common
semantic profile:
• authenticated resource schema and maximum-charge semantics;
• stable root, logical-slot, transfer, credit-generation, operation, and terminal-evidence IDs;
• immutable binding digest and the per-slot current epoch/fence;
• endpoint capability declaration;
• terminal outcomes including verified no-effect and forfeiture; and
• machine-readable reason codes for conservative refusal.

13.7 Deployment Migration
A practical rollout can proceed in increasing assurance:
(1) instrument existing agents with stable operation IDs and observed usage, making no hard-
bound claim;
(2) move counters into a durable branch ledger and reserve before effects;
(3) route high-impact effects through idempotent, queryable gateways;
(4) introduce exclusive child credits and disable copyable numeric “remaining” fields as authori-
ties;
(5) add epoch fencing, disjoint joins, reconciliation, and an independent trace verifier; and
(6) publish only claims supported by the endpoint profile actually deployed.
Legacy direct paths remain outside complete mediation until credentials and egress controls
make bypass impossible.
14 Limitations and Validity
14.1 Model Limitations
The base model assumes crash faults, authenticated records, one correct local linearization point
per branch, and a finite natural vector. It does not model Byzantine stores, signature compromise,
side channels, probabilistic settlement, debt, negative balances, interest, speculative credit, or cross-
root netting. Two independently authenticated roots are distinct authorizations; an issuer that
accidentally signs overlapping grants can overspend a real-world cap without violating either per-
root equation. Issuer-level escrow is required for an aggregate cap. The logical-atom construction
is a proof device; a faulty compression or commitment scheme can violate the implementation
mapping.
Recent work on distributed agent governance under a compromised provider studies Byzantine
replication, monitoring, auditing, and hybrid defenses [26]. Its adversary is outside our base theo-
rem: we assume correct authoritative stores, gateways, and evidence services and establish safety
only for the declared crash, retry, and partition model. The two guarantees are complementary
rather than ordered by strength.
The end-to-end effect theorem depends on sound normalization, complete mediation, an enforce-
able maximum-charge contract, gateway fencing/idempotency, and complete non-equivocating
terminal evidence. These are substantial assumptions. The ledger theorem remains useful when
some fail, but it must not be presented as conservation of actual external cost.
14.2 Formal-Method Limitations
The inductive proofs establish the mathematical transition system. TLA+/TLC and the independent
explorer cover only their declared finite constants, fault schedules, and modeled transitions. State-
space completion increases confidence in the specification and detects regressions; it is not a proof
of database durability, transport authentication, cryptographic libraries, or unmodeled adapters.
In particular, the settlement TLA+ and JavaScript encodings assign each logical unit one loca-
tion by type. Their exact-sum invariant checks transition bookkeeping but cannot represent the
duplicate-tag raw states excluded by the ownership-partition proof. The lineage encoding admits
origin-tag multiplicity and detects its compound fan-in mutant, but it is still a bounded model
rather than a mechanized proof of the full raw-relation semantics.

one local implementation and host. Model quality, real-provider accounting, Internet-scale latency,
multi-region database failover, operator response, production failure frequency, and capacity plan-
ning are separate evaluation targets.
The most important negative result is structural and does not depend on benchmark scale: with-
out endpoint cooperation, a lost response cannot distinguish non-execution from completed exe-
cution. Experiments can demonstrate the race but cannot remove it.
14.4 Construct and External Validity
“Budget” spans tokens, currency, calls, disclosures, and risk units. These dimensions differ in me-
tering authority and reversibility. Results transfer only when the deployment supplies a conser-
vative maximum and an authoritative settlement relation. Quantization can over-reserve; coarse
units trade utility for simple guarantees.
The 2026 agent papers discussed here are recent and several are preprints or an Internet-Draft.
Their reported systems and terminology may evolve. We use them to set a conservative novelty
boundary, not as proof of deployment prevalence. Classical escrow, invariant-confluence, lease,
and workflow literature remains the stronger foundation.
14.5 Internal Validity
Independent implementations, mutation tests with expected counterexamples, prefix checks,
stable result manifests, and explicit claim/evidence mapping reduce correlated specification risk
across the formal model, runtime, checker, and generated tables. Artifact results are regenerated
from source; every failed or skipped case is reported.
15 Ethics and Responsible Deployment
Budget enforcement can reduce financial loss, excessive API use, unauthorized disclosure, and
repeated high-impact effects. It can also create false confidence. A green ledger does not prove
that a planner chose a beneficial action, that a price was fair, that a recipient was appropriate,
or that complete mediation actually held. Interfaces should display endpoint profile, quarantined
capacity, unresolved effects, and assumption failures alongside a remaining balance.
Fine-grained receipts and delegation graphs reveal organizational structure, purposes, recipi-
ents, spending patterns, and potentially sensitive content. Evidence minimization, separation of
duties, access logging, encryption, retention limits, and deletion procedures are necessary. Cryp-
tographic commitments can reduce disclosure but do not make metadata harmless.
Conservative quarantine can be abused to deny service or trap a competitor’s shared capacity.
Issuers should cap the budget one child can reserve, define escalation and forfeiture authority,
record human overrides as new authorizations, and avoid automatic punitive decisions based solely
on an ambiguous external outcome or unverified assertion. The mechanism allocates authority; it
does not decide whose goals deserve resources.

16 Conclusion
Distributed agent delegation turns a budget from a number into a fault-tolerant authorization
object. Parent/child allocation inequalities, affine local types, attenuated scopes, idempotency keys,
or convergent counters each solve part of the problem. None alone prevents a refunded timeout
from colliding with a late effect, an aliased fan-in from reminting capacity, or a stale worker from
spending a reclaimed generation.
We introduced a protocol in which exclusive, labeled credit moves through a delegation lineage;
a protected effect is reserved before exposure; ambiguity is quarantined; and one idempotent ter-
minal decision applies authenticated evidence at most once. A success receipt releases only its
authenticated remainder. Full return from an exposed obligation requires a receiver-visible fence
together with authoritative proof that the exact binding was never accepted and never occurred.
The six-bucket equation keeps spendable, moving, reserved, uncertain, committed, and forfeited
rights explicit. Under stated assumptions, distinct effect instances are injectively covered, and set-
tled actual charge plus conservative outstanding exposure is bounded by the issued root vector. The
construction also preserves ledger conservation, descendant non-amplification, late-completion
safety, and partition confinement.
The central systems result is precise: local availability comes from rights allocated before a par-
tition, while uncertainty must remain charged until evidence resolves it. A system that hides this
cost by refunding on timeout does not conserve authority; it merely delays discovery of the over-
spend.
